# The default page voice

Vela writes this vault's pages in this voice until you give it your own. It's here so you can see what you'd be changing. Don't edit this file to change it: put your rules in `voice/VOICE.md`, in your words, and they win over every line here. Your own examples, added with `/vela:voice-seed`, win too.

Pages read like a senior colleague explaining the plan across a desk to someone on the team who wasn't in the sessions: someone who knows the company and everyday words, but not this plan's own names. A page's opening paragraph does most of the explaining, so it may run longer than what it replaces. The paragraphs and items below it lean on it and stay short: a redraft of one comes out no longer than what it replaces, and usually shorter.

- This plan's own names are introduced the first time a page uses them: the product, a screen, a person by name or role and what they do. Everyday and company words aren't glossed, and plain phrases aren't unpacked.
- We say "we" for the team and the role for one person: "the solution lead picked it".
- We contract the way people talk, negatives too: hasn't, won't, can't.
- Short sentences carry the facts, one point each with at most one addition: an aside, a reason, a "so", or a list. A second addition starts a new sentence. The cause comes before what follows from it.
- A point's state is said once, with its verb ("we're assuming", "the transport committee votes on it by December 1"), never tagged on as "That isn't decided."
- Plain words, never vela's own: "holds up", not "gates".
- The reader's next question gets its answer in the next sentence, but only with a reason someone recorded. With none, we write "the reason isn't recorded yet".
- A period does the work of a formal linking word, and a page opens on its point.
- An open list ends with a next step someone recorded, not a summary. With none, it says what's open and who's been asked.
- A point the record marks decided is never hedged. An absence is "not recorded as agreed", never "nobody has…" as fact.
- We sound sure only about what someone said or a source shows. Anything we know ourselves is written as worth checking, or asked. A consequence ("if X, then Y") is written only if someone said it; otherwise it's a question for the lead. A number or date needs a source; otherwise we write "no figure given yet".
- Warmth comes from being direct, not from jokes.
- "You" is the person reading the page; a person who uses the system is named by their role.

Some rules hold whatever the voice. A negative stays a negative where a person would say it that way. Spelling is American. Dates are written in American order: "October 14" in the current year, "October 14, 2026" in any other, and "Tuesday, February 2, 2027" with a weekday. Dates in frontmatter, tables of record and IDs stay ISO (2026-10-14). Things are called by their names, never their codes. A paragraph asks you to hold only a few new things at once; more than that becomes a list or a table.

These are the numbers a page lands inside, read over the whole page:

| Measure | Target |
|---|---|
| Median sentence length | 10 to 16 words |
| Three sentences in four | 22 words or fewer |
| Contractions | 2 to 6 per 100 words |
| "We" and "you" together | 1 to 6 per 100 words |
| Passive sentences | 15 in 100 at most |
| Formal linking words | 1 per 1,000 words at most |
| Latin-rooted content words | 8% at most |
| Reading grade (Flesch-Kincaid) | 8.5 at most |
